operations.comment: ; Mapper2 register values select16KiB banks; execution views record physical8KiB
; banks. CPU aliases are meaningful only in the surrounding bank context.
; Record pools: player0060, projectiles0200 stride16 (six ordinary update slots,
; seven allocation candidates), main objects0280 stride32, auxiliary0380 stride16,
; thrown object0450. Field and scratch names describe local roles; several overlays
; are intentionally shared. All physical spans have reviewed structural roles;
; unknown game meanings are described beside their established mechanics. Source/assets remain local.
; Data physical $000000..$000010. Validated iNES header: mapper 2, eight 16KiB PRG units, zero CHR units.
; Classified code physical $000010; effective8KiB context [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Dispatch the selected audio bank to its per-frame channel sequencer.
; Code physical $000013; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].

; Select a sound header from the bank0 pointer table. FE stops the auxiliary sequence and FF stops the main sequence; other requests arbitrate priority independently for the main and auxiliary channels. Bank0 must be selected.
; Code physical $000021; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; The header first byte contains separate priority nibbles. The following pointer pairs are installed into four 16-byte channel records; a lower priority request leaves the current stream running.
; Code physical $000047; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Copy the two main pointer pairs for each channel, clear its six working bytes and keep only the auxiliary flag in field10. Four records begin at RAM0400.
; Code physical $000080; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Copy one little-endian word from the request header into the current channel record. Source and destination indices advance by two.
; Code physical $000098; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Return without changing the current sequence when priority rejects a request, or after the word-copy helper completes.
; Clear the requested number of successive channel fields; the destination index points just before the first field.
; Advance the destination field and store A in the current channel record.
; Compare the high priority nibble with the active auxiliary priority. On acceptance install four auxiliary pointers, reset their slide state and leave the main stream flag intact.
; Install auxiliary pointers at record fields11/12. Empty pulse-channel streams clear their enable bit; the remaining header bytes become the shared auxiliary command cursor.
; Code physical $0000E9; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Clear the three auxiliary working fields and retain only the main flag in field10 before advancing to the next channel.
; Point the shared command cursor just beyond the four channel pointers, then reset the divider and loop count.
; Clear auxiliary priority and pointer words in all four records, then silence channels whose main pointer is also empty.
; Clear main priority and pointer words in all four records, then silence channels whose auxiliary pointer is also empty.
; Code physical $000143; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Clear the selected two-byte pointer in four 16-byte channel records. The caller chooses field0 or field11.
; Walk the channel records and their four-register APU groups. A channel is silenced only if its other stream pointer is empty.
; For the final channel disable the DMC bit through APUSTATUS; otherwise clear the current APU group timer pair. The channel countdown selects this special case.
; Classified code physical $0001B9; effective8KiB context [0, 1, 14, 15].

; Walk four 16-byte channel records at $0400 upward and four-byte APU register groups. Decrement the shared tick divider; empty sequences issue hardware updates unless their enable-mask bit suppresses them. Bank0 must be selected.
; Check the auxiliary sequence pointer at record offsets 11/12 before the main sequence at 0/1; process active channels and advance both record and APU pointers.
; Select this channel’s enable bit. The last channel uses APUSTATUS; other channels clear their timer-low register when disabled.
; Classified code physical $00020E; effective8KiB context [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Advance the record by 16 bytes and the hardware register pointer by four. Reload the shared tick divider only when it reaches zero.
; Between sequence ticks, sign-extend the slide byte at offset13 and accumulate into offset14. At a sequence tick, parse the next auxiliary audio command.
; Classified code physical $000254; effective8KiB context [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read the shared auxiliary stream when the divider expires. Bit4 selects a control command; otherwise combine two bytes into a four-fractional-bit pitch and read slide/patch fields.
; Code physical $000279; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Combine the current command and following byte, shift the pitch left four bits and store it in record fields14/15. The last channel has its own low-bit conversion.
; Read the signed slide increment and seven-bit patch index. Preserve the main-stream flag in field10, then refresh the APU registers.
; Code physical $0002D6; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; A zero pitch pair silences this channel and skips two further stream bytes without changing the current command family.
; Code physical $000304; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; The low two bits choose divider reload, counted jump, or sequence termination. This is a compact command stream, not a CPU dispatch table.
; Code physical $000310; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read the shared divider reload value and continue parsing auxiliary commands.
; Read a repeat count and absolute little-endian target. While the shared count has not reached the limit, install that target; otherwise reset the count and skip it. A zero limit always jumps.
; Clear this record auxiliary pointer and shared priority/reload state. Back up the command cursor by one before returning.
; Code physical $000371; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Return the next auxiliary command byte in A and X, advancing the shared little-endian cursor with carry.
; Code physical $000385; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Select a three-byte register patch by field10 low seven bits. Combine its timer-high bits with the 12-bit integer part of record14/15, whose low nibble is fractional pitch.
; Classified code physical $0003EC; effective8KiB context [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Flag7 at channel offset10 enables an extra duration update on odd audio frames. Offset6 counts in steps of two; zero clears the high flag before parsing the next main audio command.
; Clear the fast-tick flag and parse the next note/control byte. Low five bits select note, rest or command; upper bits choose a duration from the bank0 table.
; Command30 sets the field10 sign flag and resumes parsing. Other notes update duration and pitch unless the auxiliary stream owns this channel.
; For the last channel use the note low nibble directly. Other channels index a little-endian pitch table through record fields7/8, then write the selected register patch.
; Code physical $0004A0; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Set field10 bit7 and continue parsing immediately. The per-frame entry can then advance the duration twice on alternating frames.
; Set duration from the upper command bits. If auxiliary audio does not own the channel, disable or zero its timer and update the APU patch.
; Mask the command to eight slots and use the inline address-minus-one table through a synthetic RTS. Slots4/5 are zero and their natural selection remains unresolved; table bytes are data.

; Data physical $0004E7..$0004F7. Eight little-endian address-minus-one words used by DispatchInlineAudioCommand. Slots4 and5 are zero; the masked selector alone does not prove those slots are naturally selected.
; Code physical $0004F7; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read the low/high patch pointer into record fields2/3 and resume the main stream parser.
; Code physical $000501; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read the register-patch index into record field4 and resume parsing.
; Code physical $00050B; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read a pitch-table selector and store base863F plus twice that selector into record fields7/8. This selects a word-aligned pitch source.
; Use record field9 as a repeat counter, then read an absolute stream pointer. Zero repeats always jump; a completed count resets the counter and skips the pointer.
; Code physical $00056A; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read a packed note/duration byte using the alternate duration table at8637, then reuse the note/rest paths.
; Code physical $000585; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Clear this record main cursor and global main priority. Silence only when the auxiliary enable bit does not retain ownership.
; Code physical $00059E; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Read a byte through the cursor in record fields0/1, return it in A and X, and write the incremented cursor back with carry.
; Pop the caller return address, select one inline little-endian address-minus-one word using X, push its high/low bytes and RTS into that handler. The table is not executable fallthrough.
; Code physical $0005D9; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Multiply A by the channel duration factor in field5 using repeated addition and store the byte result in field6. A zero factor wraps the eight-bit loop.
; Code physical $0005F0; effective 8KiB banks [0, 1, 14, 15].
; Select a three-byte patch through record fields2/3 and field4. Write its first two registers, then merge its timer-high bits with fields14/15.
